{{Short description|Japanese Buddhist musical narrative}}{{Japanese Buddhism}}
{{nihongo|'''''Kōshiki'''''|講式|lead=yes}} is a musical genre used in [[Buddhism in Japan|Japanese Buddhism]] rituals. It originated from the [[Tendai]] belief in the late tenth century, and later spread to other Buddhist schools.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-10-05 |title=Memory, Music, Manuscripts: The Ritual Dynamics of ''Kōshiki'' in Japanese ''Sōtō Zen'' |url=https://uhpress.hawaii.edu/title/memory-music-manuscripts-the-ritual-dynamics-of-koshiki-in-japanese-soto-zen/ |access-date=2023-10-24 |website=UH Press |language=en-US}}</ref> It is a form of narrative music,<ref name="ambros-2016a" /><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Ambros |first=Barbara R. |date=2016-03-22 |title=A rite of their own: Japanese Buddhist nuns and the ''Anan kōshiki'' |url=https://go.gale.com/ps/i.do?p=AONE&sw=w&issn=03041042&v=2.1&it=r&id=GALE%7CA460507213&sid=googleScholar&linkaccess=abs |journal=Japanese Journal of Religious Studies |language=English |volume=43 |issue=1 |pages=207–251|doi=10.18874/jjrs.43.1.2016.207-250 |doi-access=free }}</ref> and often incorporates foreign non-Buddhist [[Deity|deities]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Guelberg |first=Niels |date=2016-03-22 |title=''Jingi Koshiki'': a neglected field of study |url=https://go.gale.com/ps/i.do?p=AONE&sw=w&issn=03041042&v=2.1&it=r&id=GALE%7CA460507217&sid=googleScholar&linkaccess=abs |journal=Japanese Journal of Religious Studies |language=English |volume=43 |issue=1 |pages=153–176|doi=10.18874/jjrs.43.1.2016.153-175 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

The word "kōshiki" literally translates to "[[Kō (lecture)|lecture]] ceremony." 

== Origins ==
The exact beginnings of ''kōshiki'' are unclear. The earliest known work in the genre is "''Nijügo zanmai shiki''", written by [[Genshin]] in 986. This work became a model for future works in the style. By the 12th and 13th centuries, ''kōshiki'' became popular among many Japanese Buddhists.<ref name="ambros-2016a">{{Cite journal |last1=Ambros |first1=Barbara R. |last2=Ford |first2=James L. |last3=Mross |first3=Michaela |date=2016 |title=Editors' Introduction: "''Kōshiki''" in Japanese Buddhism |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/43869083 |journal=Japanese Journal of Religious Studies |volume=43 |issue=1 |pages=1–15 |jstor=43869083 |issn=0304-1042}}</ref>

== Form ==
''Kōshiki'' is a liturgical ritual performance, which talks about an object of devotion. The object's history, virtues, and importance are described, and the ritual connects object with those present for the performance.<ref name="ambros-2016a" />

The general structure of ''kōshiki'' begins with an intention statement, followed by prose sections. The prose sections discuss the intention statement, and are sometimes in Chinese. Each section finishes by [[Transfer of merit|transferring merit]].<ref name="ambros-2016a" /> A work of ''kōshiki'' ends with a chant or verse about the theme.
